commits.message:
expectLinearTime returns the size it measured at, so its own stall tests fail rather than pass vacuously when a faster runner grows the size (rich-unfiled-791c.sx9g)

The unmeasurable message says to pass a larger size again: linear work given
a size more than 64 times too small fails with it too. The escalation tests
pin the sizes tried to the x4 sequence.
expectLinearTime takes a larger size itself when the smaller run is under the floor, so a faster runner cannot fail linear work (rich-unfiled-791c.sx9g)

A declared width and a noWrap column too wide for the table are cut evenly together, as Rich's are (rich-unfiled-791c.py6q) (#474)

* A declared width and a noWrap column too wide for the table are cut evenly together, as Rich's last-resort ratio_reduce cuts them (rich-unfiled-791c.py6q)

layoutTable paid every reservation before any minimum, so a noWrap column
beside a declared width gave up all its cells alone. A declared width is now
a minimum that weighs nothing, and the one minimum pass cuts the wrapping
columns first and then every column evenly. Pinned against Rich 15 in
table-squeeze.golden.txt.

* A ratio column's declared width is held to the table as any declared width is, and the even cut is described as Rich's is (rich-unfiled-791c.py6q)

High review of PR #474. A ratio column with a width wider than the table took
every cell of the even cut and left a declared neighbour none; Rich 15 holds
it with with_maximum(max_width) and draws [14, 3] at width 20. One declared()
now holds every declared width. The prose promised no column is cut to nothing
while another keeps cells; Rich's ratio_reduce does exactly that, so the prose
changes, not the cut. Two new golden sweeps pin wrap-first-then-even order.

* Every ratio floor is held to the table, its minWidth included (rich-unfiled-791c.py6q)

Medium review of PR #474: a noWrap ratio column flooring at minWidth: 30 still
took every cell of the even cut from a declared neighbour. Rich's expand path,
the model this port's ratio follows, ignores min_width there and keeps the
declared column whole; holding the floor brings the cut to [14, 3] and drops
the width-or-minWidth branch.
